observations.result: Ten events in nine participants; reported resolved; two events caused treatment discontinuation. This is an exposed-cohort proportion, not a controlled excess-risk estimate.

methods_and_limits.text: Integration and NfL subgrouping were described as prespecified before initial VALOR database lock. Full-ITT NfL-adjusted testing was added after original analyses. Integrated SAP versions: June 8, 2021 to September 12, 2024; not the standalone OLE protocol.
NfL-defined subgroups differ from the original primary population defined using variant and prerandomization slope. Do not equate them.
Week 148 used assessment availability (at least 40% across combined groups) and scheduling. Multiple imputation and reference-based sensitivity analyses were used. Attrition remains important.
The supplement warns that estimates after week 192 are unreliable because numbers at risk fall. Do not interpret subgroup median differences as a precise causal survival extension.
Small sample, crossover and limited power constrain conclusions. Follow-up does not replace the original randomized primary analysis or establish benefit for all ALS.

The publisher Table 2 has an impossible negative upper confidence limit for slower-subgroup death; Figure 2 has nonmonotone ITT delayed-group risk counts. These entries were not extracted or silently repaired. They leave source-level uncertainty beyond the selected concordant estimates.
